title: Relate Fractions, Decimals, and Percentages
objective: I can write equivalent fractions, decimals, and percents for the same value.
model: one amount shown as a fraction bar, a 100-grid and a 0-1 number line, with the denominator scaled to 100 to read the percent

widgets.component: slider 0-100 plus seven benchmark buttons driving a fraction bar, a 0 / 0.25 / 0.5 / 0.75 / 1 scale, a 100-grid and three live tiles (Fraction, Decimal, Percent)
widgets.root: The meter itself is manipulable, but every task calls setT1Value(task.val), so the three tiles beside the question already print the fraction, decimal and percent of the value in the task (tasks 2, 3, 5, 6, 7, 8). The answer is on screen before the student thinks.
widgets.replacement: Hide the three tiles while a task is open (keep the bar, the 100-grid and the scale). Turn each task into a build: 'Slide the meter to 3/4 of the bar', check by the bar and grid reading, then the student types the decimal and the percent. Show the trio tiles only after Check, or in free-explore mode when no task is active.

widgets.where: Practice Tab 1 tasks 1-8 (2 mc, 3 single, 2 dual, 1 single)
widgets.root: Content is on objective, but with the tiles visible the task is transcription. Tasks 1 and 4 also offer the answer pair as a choice.
widgets.replacement: Same replacement as the meter row: tiles hidden, student sets and reads the meter, typed answers only.

widgets.component: fraction -> equivalent fraction out of 100 (scale factor) -> decimal -> percent; from problem 2 the last step is a 'what does it mean' sentence choice
widgets.root: Scaling the denominator to 100 is the lesson's worked example (3/4 = 75/100 = 0.75 = 75%); denominators 2, 4, 5, 10, 20, 25, 50 only, so every factor is whole and the decimal is exact. The meaning check removes the copy step.

widgets.where: Practice Tab 3 (8: given a decimal, a percent or a fraction, supply the other two)
widgets.root: All eight values and simplified fractions verified (7/20, 13/20, 0.375 = 37.5%, 2/25, 11/25, 1/8 = 12.5%, 17/20, 0.72 = 72%); includes the divide-numerator-by-denominator route the keyIdea names.

widgets.where: Practice Tab 4 (8 mc: food drive, sleepy animals, giraffe, two error detectives, free throws, ordering mixed forms, 30% off as a fraction)
widgets.component: word problems and error analysis for the three forms
widgets.root: Keys correct (3/4 / 0.75 / 75%, tiger 65% versus 40%, 8% and 0.08, 6 hundredths not 6 tenths, 9/20 = 45%, 70% versus 68%, 35% < 0.4 < 1/2, 3/10). Distractor 2 of problem 2 ('2/5 = 50%') is wrong by design.

widgets.where: Practice Bonus Round (gen fdp, 4 rounds of 1/2, 3/4, 1/5 … 17/20, 18/25)
widgets.component: 'Match the Trios': fraction, decimal and percent tiles of the same value
widgets.root: For this lesson the match is the idea: each trio needs a conversion (17/20, 0.85, 85%), tiles are generated from the numbers so a label cannot disagree with its trio, a miss shows no answer, no timer.

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 1 (8: 175%, 250%, 0.4%, 0.25% to a fraction, 3.25, 0.008, 2 1/5, largest near 1%)
widgets.component: typed conversions of values above 100% and below 1%, no figure
widgets.root: Eight conversions of one value into its other forms with no model: no number line, no grid and no bar. The lesson's idea is a representation the student should be able to move on, and above 100% or below 1% is exactly where the picture is hardest to hold.
widgets.replacement: Add a rescalable number line to the page: a movable point on 0-1 that the student drags to the given value (175% needs the line to extend to 2; 0.4% needs a 100× zoom window with the 0 to 1% stretch shown), tiles hidden; the student drags first, then types the other two forms. Show 0.4 and 0.4% as two points on one line to trap '0.4% = 0.4'.

widgets.component: decimal and percent by dividing, simplifying first, repeating decimals rounded to a tenth of a percent
widgets.root: The 'divide numerator by denominator' route in the keyIdea, with simplification as the bridge; all answers verified (0.1875 = 18.75%, 0.175 = 17.5%, 0.333 = 33.3%, 0.667 = 66.7%).

widgets.component: convert the given form to the other two, simplified
widgets.root: Same typed-conversion worksheet as Tab 1 with no representation.
widgets.replacement: Same number-line rebuild as Tab 1: the given value is placed for the student on a rescalable line and the student names the other two forms from the line; for 0.005 and 0.0025 the zoom window is the scaffold.

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 4 items t4_1, t4_3, t4_6, t4_7 (animal sleep order, cow 16.5%, 5/16 liter, 0.5% versus 1/2)
widgets.root: Conversions only; keys verified (Python 75% > Tiger 65% > Chimpanzee 40% > Giraffe 8%; 0.165 = 33/200; 31.25%; 1/200).

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 4 items t4_4, t4_5, t4_8 (25% then 20% off, 0.75% of 200 g, 225% of 80 MW)
widgets.component: consecutive discounts and 'percent of a quantity'
widgets.root: Taking a percent of a number (Part = Percent × Whole, discounts) is lesson 4-4; successive discounts are in no Unit 4 lesson. 4-2 asks only for equivalent forms.
widgets.replacement: Replace with conversion-only items: 'A sports drink is 0.75% electrolytes: write it as a decimal and a fraction', 'a plant produced 2.25 times its target: what percent?', 'Jordan says 25% off and then 20% off is 45%: write each discount as a fraction and decimal and say which is bigger' (no totals).

widgets.where: Challenge Tab 5 (10 mc quiz) and Bonus Round (fdp rounds 5/4, 3/2, 7/4 … 1/200, 3/500, 1/400, 9/8, 11/16, 13/20)
widgets.root: On objective; keys verified (including 0.833… ≈ 83.3% for 5/6). Matching 1/200, 3/500, 1/400 forces real conversions.

formulaOrder.formula: Part = Percent × Whole (percent of a quantity)
